newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end little changed after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end little changed after volatile day.

text.p: Swiss shares closed little changed after a roller-coaster day as the blue chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) hit an early high of 5,835,6 points, dipped to a low of 5,723.6 and finally ended mid-range.
Dealers described the market as volatile and nervous, although basic sentiment remained positive, they said.
The SMI lost 0.1 percent or 5.8 points to close at 5,765.2.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index dipped 0.12 percent or 4.56 points below its Monday's close to 3,681.31.
Losses in bourse heavy-weight UBS UBS, which fell 2.5 percent or 41 francs to 1.627 after reporting first half results, helped to set the tone in the morning.
Profit-taking set in after the bank announced a 67.4 percent rise in first half net profit to a record 1.86 billion Swiss francs.
In contrast, registered shares of SBC posted gains on expectations of higher profit. The share jumped eight francs to 408. SBC will report results on August 13.
CS Group closed marginally lower at 196 francs, down 0.75 francs. CS will report on August 27.
Shares of insurer Winterthur rose on buying by BZ Bank, traders said. The stock soared 24 francs to 1,493.

A one percent drop in Novartis shares also depressed Swiss stocks, while chemical and pharmaceutical stocks were mixed. Novartis lost 28 francs to 2,325. The positive expectations for its new medicine Exelon for treatment of Alzheimer was not reflected in the price, one dealer said.

ABB was strongly sought, with the bearer share advancing 34 francs to 2,169 and the registered share rising 10 francs to 428. Dealers mentioned rumours about a unitary share in connection with ABB's first half results due on Thursday.
Nestle, SMH and Alusuisse profited from the strong dollar. Nestle rose 24 francs and closed at 1,924.
Swiss watchmaker SMH was up 2.25 francs at 208.25.
